title: Classifying noncompact groups over Hausdorff bases
statement: Construct a category of principal bundles over Hausdorff bases and universal objects that agree with ordinary bundles over completely regular bases while retaining characteristic information about a noncompact linear Lie group beyond the ordinary homotopy type of \(BG\).
status: As of November 2026, the specified linear-group programme is answered by \citet[\S\S1--2 and4]{gelfandfuchs1967topology}. The more general elementary-object formulation is treated by \citet[Theorems1--2]{gelfandfuchs1968classifying}, with stronger axioms than the notebook sketch.

title: Common fixed and periodic points of commuting interval maps
statement: Do two commuting continuous maps \([0,1]\to[0,1]\) necessarily share a fixed point? The accompanying differentiable statement asks for a fixed point of one map that is periodic for the other.
status: As of November 2026, the common-fixed-point assertion is false: the Boyce and Huneke counterexamples circulated in1967 and appeared in print in1969. A \(C^1\) map commuting with a continuous map has the fixed/periodic point described by Schwartz1965. The latter precise formulation was checked indirectly in \citet[Introduction]{alikhanikoopaei1998commuting}. This index entry does not add the different all-continuous common-periodic-point conjecture, which the notebook does not ask.

title: Metric classification of hyperbolic two-torus automorphisms
statement: When are two hyperbolic automorphisms of \(\mathbb T^2\), with Haar probability, isomorphic by an invertible measure-preserving conjugacy modulo zero?
status: As of November 2026, equality of entropy is necessary and sufficient by \citet[Main Theorem]{adlerweiss1967entropy}. The paper was communicated24April1967 and publishedJune1967, before both notebook occurrences. The four-block recoding and geometric component refinement in these notes match its proof exactly.

title: Algebraic classification of Anosov diffeomorphisms
statement: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov automorphism of an infranilmanifold?
status: As of November 2026, the general conjecture remains open. The known infranilmanifold case is the Franks--Manning theorem; the two-torus case is proved in \citet[Theorem5.2]{sinai1968markov}. See the precise conjecture and known case in \citet[Conjecture2.3, Theorem2.4]{spatzier2016rigidity} and its still-conjectural status in \citet[\S2]{damjanovic2026symmetries}.
